newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia-Thai oil well drilling completed.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia-Thai oil well drilling completed.

text.p: The Malaysia-Thailand Joint Authority (MTJA) said on Thursday that its contractors have completed drilling and testing on a wildcat well in a joint development area.

The tests yielded a combined gas flow rate of 48 million standard cubic feet per day, 1,451 barrels per day (bpd) of condensate (55 degrees API gravity), and 585 bpd of oil (41 degrees API gravity) measured through choke size of 36/64-52/64 inches, the authority said in a statement.
The statement said the Well Jengka-1 was spudded on January 21 and was drilled to a total depth of 2,822 metres (9,256 feet) to test the hydrocarbon potential of the Jengka Prospect in Block B-17.
Contractors of the block are PTTEP International Ltd and Petronas Carigali (JDA) Sdn Bhd, the exploration arm of Malaysian state oil firm Petronas.
Four drill stem tests were conducted over the depth intervals' range of 1,892 metres to 2,182 metres subsea.
The MTJA is a statutory body vested with the exclusive rights to explore and exploit petroleum resources in the joint development area of Malaysia and Thailand.
